clips.send: Date. Is it current enough for your question? Science, health and technology change fast: prefer recent sources. For history, an old source can be gold: it may be a primary source from the time. Watch for old news shared as if it were new. Old isn’t bad; out of date is. The date a post was shared is not always the date it was written.

clips.send: Images can lie too. Edited, staged or out-of-context pictures. Check shadows, reflections, repeated patterns and edges that look cut out. Most misleading photos are real but used with a false caption. A reverse image search shows where a picture first appeared. Ask: what is outside the frame? Photo editing is older than computers: Soviet officials erased people from photos in the 1930s.

clips.send: Lateral reading. Leave the site to check the site. Open a new tab and search the organization’s name. What do others say about it? A site’s own “About us” page can say anything it wants. SIFT: Stop, Investigate the source, Find better coverage, Trace claims to the original. Don’t read deeper; read wider. A professional-looking website is not proof of reliability.

clips.send: Evidence. Does it show where the facts came from? Good sources cite studies, data and experts you can check yourself. Trace a claim to its original source: who first said it? One personal story is not evidence for everyone. No sources? No trust. Links that just lead to other copies of the same story are not independent evidence (circular reporting).

clips.send: Purpose. To inform, persuade, entertain or sell? A company page about its own product wants to sell, so expect one side only. “Sponsored content” and “paid post” mean someone paid for it: an ad dressed as news. Satire sites (labeled humor) are jokes, not news. Follow the money: who benefits if I believe this? Persuasive isn’t automatically false, but you must check its evidence.

clips.send: Author. Who made this, and do they know the subject? Look for a name and credentials: a doctor writing about health, a scientist about science. No author at all is a warning sign. Expert in one thing is not equal to expert in everything: a famous athlete is not a nutrition expert. Who says so, and why should I believe them? Lots of followers is not equal to expertise.

clips.send: 图片也会说谎。被修改、摆拍或断章取义的图片。检查影子、倒影、重复的图案和像是剪贴上去的边缘。大多数误导人的照片是真的，只是配了错误的说明。反向图片搜索能找出图片最早出现在哪里。问问自己：画面之外还有什么？修改照片比电脑还早：20 世纪 30 年代苏联就从照片里抹掉过人。

clips.send: 日期（When?）。对你的问题来说，够新吗？科学、健康和技术变化很快：尽量用新的资料。研究历史时，老资料可能是宝贝：它可能是当时留下的一手资料。小心有人把旧新闻当新新闻转发。旧不等于坏，过时才是问题。帖子被转发的日期不一定是写作的日期。

clips.send: 作者（Who?）。谁写的？他懂这个领域吗？找名字和资历：医生写健康，科学家写科学。完全没有作者是一个警告信号。某方面的专家不等于什么都懂：著名运动员不一定是营养专家。谁说的？我凭什么相信他？粉丝多不等于专业。

clips.send: 证据（How do they know?）。它说明事实从哪里来了吗？好的来源会引用你能自己核查的研究、数据和专家。把一个说法追溯到最初的来源：最早是谁说的？一个人的亲身经历不能代表所有人。没有出处？不要轻信。只链接到同一个故事的其他转载，不算独立证据（循环报道）。

clips.send: 目的（Why?）。为了告知、说服、娱乐，还是推销？公司介绍自家产品的页面是为了卖东西，只会说好话。“Sponsored content（赞助内容）”“paid post（付费帖子）”说明有人付了钱：这是穿着新闻外衣的广告。讽刺网站（标着“幽默”）是开玩笑，不是新闻。顺着钱找：如果我相信了，谁得好处？有说服目的不一定是假的，但必须检查它的证据。

clips.send: 横向阅读。离开网站，去核查网站。打开新标签页，搜索这个机构的名字：别人怎么评价它？网站自己的“关于我们”想怎么写就怎么写。SIFT：停一停 · 调查来源 · 寻找更好的报道 · 追溯原始出处。别往深里读，要往宽里读。网站看起来很专业，不能证明它可靠。
